<summary>Agent "Investigate missing upgrade proposal" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>**Short answer.** This is mostly by design plus once-only latches, not a crash. There is one real gap: a pending upgrade is announced at most once and is never repeated while the project stays behind. I could not replay the original failure, because the other agent had already applied the upgrade. `ddflow upgrade --status` now reports "project stamp 0.2.1, plan: up to date, last upgrade 0.1.10 -> 0.2.1 (10:07)". The timeline below is reconstructed from the marker files and the code.

**Not the cause**
- `DDFLOW_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` and `release_check`: `release-check.json` shows a check at 10:04. That check only proposes a newer ddflow release, and newest equals running at 0.2.1, so it never fires here.
- Version skew: the `[REDACTED:path]` launcher runs the dev checkout, as its header says. The hooks use `[REDACTED:path]` plus `PYTHONPATH`. Both report 0.2.1, so there is no uv-run versus installed mismatch.
- Worktrees: `repo` resolves to the primary checkout (`mcp.py` ~511 and ~1596), so the markers are shared and the worktree is irrelevant.
- The stamp gap does take the "behind" path: `_decide` (`upgrade_start.py:394-412`) finds the project at 0.1.10 and running at 0.2.1, so it goes to `_behind_report`.

**Why nothing was applied (by design)**
- `upgrade_start.py:268` applies safe categories only when `surf == "container"`. An MCP start outside a container only rebuilds the index and proposes; `:13-16` cites D-upgrade-on-mcp-connect.
- `[upgrade].auto = "check"` makes `UN.line` a notice only (`upgrade_notice.py:~125`). It applies only when `auto = "safe"`.

**Why no proposal appeared (latches already used up)**
1. **Per-machine notice latch.** `upgrade-notice.json` holds `"Upgraded ddflow 0.1.10 -> 0.2.1: run ddflow upgrade --plan"`, written 2026-10-09 13:03. `UN.line` returns "" whenever `told >= running` (`upgrade_notice.py:~128-131`). It sets that mark before building the plan, and the text says "Upgraded" although nothing was applied. That one line was consumed on Oct 9 and never repeats.
2. **Start-marker `briefed` latch.** `take_for_brief` (`upgrade_start.py:~500-520`) returns an APPLIED or PROPOSED text once, then returns "" when `briefed` is true. Only UNFINISHED statuses repeat (`_repeats`, `:~456`). The text embeds the item count, so it only re-arms when the count changes. The marker at 10:07:16 shows 72 items with `briefed:false`.
3. **Per-process handshake cache.** `_START_REPORTS` (`api/setup.py:~702`) means a long-lived MCP server reports once per process. That 10:07 marker has no `key`, `complete` or `repeat` fields, so it was written by a process still running pre-fix code. This matches that process having imported its code before the B-start-timeout fix commits of Oct 11 (4149efcf and later).
4. **No other surface repeats it.** `doctor_notes` only covers TIMEOUT and FAILED, so `doctor` and `status` never repeat a pending proposal.

chunk_findings.detail: The change fixes three independent suppression mechanisms (the `take_for_brief` briefed latch, the `upgrade_notice` per-machine "told" latch at ~125-131, and the per-process `_START_REPORTS` cache in `api/setup.py`), but this regression test never performs the "mark the notice told" step that the change's own test plan specifies, and it only drives `US.start` / `US.take_for_brief` / `US.doctor_notes` — never the `upgrade_notice` latch surface and never a long-lived process that would hit the `_START_REPORTS` cache. Concretely, if someone re-introduces the `upgrade_notice` behaviour that "marks told before the plan is built" (so the proposal is announced once at the machine level and then suppressed even though `_behind` is still true), the three assertions `first == second == third == rep["text"]` and `doctor_notes(...) == [rep["text"]]` still pass, because the test never sets or observes that latch; likewise a regression in the per-process `_START_REPORTS` cache is invisible here since every call is either a direct service call or a fresh CLI process. The test therefore does not guard the bug end-to-end as the described regression scenario requires.

data.body: Operator 2026-10-12, from the home-simulator upgrade: phase PHASE-39-FOLLOW-UPS-NOT and tasks P42.8.give-base-room-bluep and P42.8.model-alexas-cloud-g have mangled (truncated) ids; ddflow has no way to rename an id or move a task to another phase, so the upgrade agent left them. Add the means to correct such records: rename an id of any kind (phase, task, bug, decision, lesson, research...) with every reference rewritten (needs, parent, phase, gates, leases, links, bugs fix-<id>, worktree/branch names); move a task (and its sub-tasks) to another phase; reorder phases and tasks; and a repair the upgrade can propose for truncated ids. The event log is append-only and committed, so all of it must be new events folded by the model, never an edit of history.

Decide the behaviour for claimed items, merged branches and a concurrent clone that still uses the old id.
